name.value: UNO Flip!: My Hero Academia (McDonald's Happy Meal Edition)

item.description:
This is a double-sided promotional card game released globally as part of the 2026 McDonald's "UNO x Anime" Happy Meal crossover campaign. Packed inside an explosive orange and black box featuring Katsuki Bakugo unleasing an explosion, this licensed travel-sized mini-deck brings the UNO Flip! mechanics into the superhuman world of Quirks across an optimized 43-card format tailored for 2 to 4 players.
The game utilizes two distinct playable sides reflecting the eternal struggle between Heroes and Villains: the "Light Side" (white borders), which features the students of U.A. High School training and working together, and the punishing "Dark Side" (black borders), which turns the tables to feature the dangerous League of Villains. When a "Flip" card is played, all players must instantly turn over their hands, the draw pile, and the discard pile to activate severe Dark Side penalties like "Draw 5" and "Skip Everyone."
This set features a franchise-exclusive holographic foil "Howitzer Impact" Wild Card. When played on either side, it triggers Bakugo's explosive combat drive: the active player chooses the next color to continue play, and then forces the next player in turn order to instantly reveal cards from the draw deck one by one until they pull a card matching that chosen color, adding all revealed non-matching cards directly into their hand.

item.description:
This is a double-sided promotional card game released globally as part of the 2026 McDonald's "UNO x Anime" Happy Meal crossover campaign. Housed in a dark teal/blue box featuring Sasuke Uchiha wielding his Chidori, this licensed travel-sized mini-deck adapts the popular UNO Flip! mechanics into an optimized 43-card format designed for 2 to 4 players.
The game utilizes two distinct playable sides: the "Light Side" (white borders), which features standard gameplay with heroes from Konoha like Naruto and Sakura, and the punishing "Dark Side" (black borders), which shifts focus to villains and rogue shinobi like Orochimaru and the Akatsuki. When a "Flip" card is played, all players must instantly turn over their hand cards, the draw pile, and the discard pile to unleash much more aggressive action penalties, such as "Draw 5" and "Skip Everyone."
This set features a franchise-exclusive holographic foil "Amaterasu / Eternal Mangekyo" Wild Card. When played on the Dark Side, it allows the active player to change the color and force an opponent to "burn" a card from their hand—permanently removing it from the round directly to the bottom of the draw pile—while skipping that opponent's next turn.

item.description:
This is a double-sided promotional card game released globally as part of the 2026 McDonald's "UNO x Anime" Happy Meal crossover campaign. Packed inside a vibrant pink box featuring the energetic Anya Forger, this licensed travel-sized mini-deck brings the UNO Flip! mechanic to the world of Ostania across an optimized 43-card format tailored for 2 to 4 players.
The game utilizes two distinct playable sides that mirror the dual natures of the characters: the "Light Side" (white borders), which highlights everyday family life with cute character illustrations of Anya, Bond, and school classmates, and the "Dark Side" (black borders), which plunges players into the secret underworld featuring Twilight's espionage missions and Thorn Princess's assassination targets. Playing a "Flip" card forces all players to instantly flip their hands and the draw piles over, unlocking much harsher action penalties like "Draw 5" and "Skip Everyone."
This set features a franchise-exclusive holographic foil "Starlight Anya" Wild Card. When played, the active player chooses the next color and immediately awards themselves a "Starlight." In gameplay terms, this allows the player to select any opponent and force them to play the rest of the current round with their hand completely revealed face-up on the table, simulating Anya reading their mind to predict their next moves.

UNO FLIP! flips classic UNO game play with twists like a double-sided deck, special FLIP card and tougher penalties that add a competitive edge…and with a theme inspired by the supernatural TV thriller Stranger Things, fans will really flip over this edition! There is a "Real World" side to the deck, which plays like the classic UNO game, and an "Upside Down" side where penalties are super-tough. Play the FLIP card, and all cards in the player's hand, the draw pile and draw deck are flipped over to reveal an entirely new set of numbers and colors on the opposite side. The holder of the FLIP card determines which side to play -- and when cards are switched back around. The "Upside Down" side of the deck includes action cards that really shake things up, like Draw Five and Skip Everyone. Strategize to rattle the competition and be the first to get rid of all cards to win. When players are down to one card, they still can't forget to shout "UNO!" This fun family card game is perfect for 2 to 10 players ages 7 years old and up, especially fans of the show. Colors and decorations may vary.

item.description:
This version of UNO includes transparent, waterproof cards similar to UNO H2O and a special Whirlpool device. The Whirlpool has random effects that appear when shook (it works like a Magic 8-Ball).
The rules are simplified. For example, the winner conditions are no longer points based. The first player to win three hands wins the game. Also gone are rules regarding playing Wild Draw 4 Cards when you can play another card.
The Whirlpool is activated by playing a special Splash card or playing a 0 or a 2. The next player must then shake the Whirlpool and follow the results: 1) Draw H2O - draw until they get a blue, 2, 0 or wild card. 2) Wave Right - show a card to the player on the right. 3) Wave Left - show a card to the player on the left. 4) Wipeout - reverse order of play (player who started the Splash must use the whirlpool)
Other possible Whirlpool results are draw, discard and give cards.
The cards and Whirlpool are contained in a sturdy plastic box, with a slide on/off lid.

item.description:
This is the original Uno Card game with three new ways to play. Mattel had a contest to see what "House Rules" people used and added the three best variations. The Variants are as follows.
Jump-In Uno: In this variation a player can assume control of the game if they have the exact same card that is on top of the discard pile. (This was the first place winner submited by Wess Eslinger.) Seven-O Uno: This involves passing your hands to other players when certain cards are played. (This was the second place winner submitted by Sarah Petite.) Progressive Uno: If a draw card is played then the "victim" can play the same type of card thus passing the result on to the next player. (This was the third place winner submitted by Douglas Temple.)

item.description:
UNO Madness is an implementation of the classic card game UNO with a mechanical gimmick. The game is played on a spring-mounted tray. After latching, the tray springs when a mechanical timer expires. The tray has 24 slots lined in a spiral path; the final slot (in the centre) is labeled with the word UNO.
At the start of the game, the tray is latched and the timer wound up. Each player draws five tiles and keep their hand secret from the others. The first player places a numbered tile in the first slot on the tray and starts the timer. Continuing with the next player in sequence, the players follow the standard UNO rules in playing their tiles (color succeeds color, number succeeds number, draw when unable to play, etc). They also have to say "Madness" to signify the end of their turn.
Play stops when a player has played his or her last tile, has played a tile on the last slot, or when the timer expires. In the first two cases, the player records his score (according to UNO rules, summing up values of the tiles in other players' hands) and the game is reset (tiles reshuffled and redrawn, etc). For the last case, everybody keeps their hand and the player who has yet to finish his or her turn when the board has sprung draws four more tiles. Play then continues. The game ends after a certain accumulated score has been reached or a certain number of rounds have been played.
